input: Customer says: 'My order is late, this is unacceptable. I needed it for a wedding.'
expected: Empathetic apology, offer to check current delivery status, ask for the order number, do not promise a discount.

input: Customer says: 'I received the wrong item in my package.'
expected: Apology, offer a return label, offer to ship the correct item, ask for order details and a photo.

input: Customer says: 'I want a refund for the headphones I bought last week.'
expected: Confirm willingness to help, ask for the order number, mention the refund window policy, set expectations on timing.

input: Customer says: 'I bought this 90 days ago and want to return it. It still has tags.'
expected: Empathetic acknowledgement, explain the 30 day return window politely, offer alternatives like store credit if available, do not promise a full refund.

input: Customer says: 'help'
expected: Polite request for more information, offer common help topics, no assumptions or invented order details.

input: Customer says: 'my odrr didnt arrve and i nedd it'
expected: Acknowledge the issue despite typos, ask for the order number, offer to track the delivery, do not invent order details.

input: Customer says: 'My package never arrived but the tracking says delivered.'
expected: Empathetic acknowledgement, offer to investigate with the carrier, ask the customer to check with neighbors and the address, mention a missing package claim as a next step, do not promise a refund yet.

input: Customer says: 'Tracking shows my order is stuck at the depot for 5 days.'
expected: Apology for the delay, offer to contact the carrier, set expectations for response time, ask for the order number.

input: Customer says: 'I am in Germany and want to return my order. Do you cover return shipping internationally?'
expected: Polite acknowledgement, explain that international returns may not include prepaid shipping, offer to confirm the exact policy after looking up the order, do not invent a free return shipping promise.

input: Customer says: 'This was a gift and I lost the receipt. Can I still return it?'
expected: Empathetic acknowledgement, explain the gift return process if available, ask for any details that might help locate the order, do not promise a refund without verification.

input: Customer says: 'I want to cancel my subscription immediately.'
expected: Confirm the cancellation request, ask for the account email, explain the cancellation process and any prorated billing, do not invent retention discounts.

input: Customer says: 'Cancel my order, it has not shipped yet.'
expected: Acknowledge the request, offer to check the shipment status, explain that cancellation may not be possible if already in fulfillment, ask for the order number.

input: Customer says: 'I was charged twice for the same order on my credit card.'
expected: Apology, offer to investigate the duplicate charge, ask for the last four digits and the order number, set expectations for the refund timeline if confirmed.

input: Customer says: 'There is a charge on my card I do not recognize from your store.'
expected: Acknowledge the concern, offer to look up the charge, ask for the date and amount, do not confirm or deny the charge without verification.

input: Customer says: 'I want to upgrade my subscription from basic to premium.'
expected: Confirm the upgrade request, explain the cost difference and proration, ask for the account email to process the change.

input: Customer says: 'Why was I billed on the 3rd? My subscription started on the 15th.'
expected: Acknowledge the confusion, offer to look up the account billing cycle, explain that the renewal date may differ from the sign up date, ask for the account email.

input: Customer says: 'My new TV arrived with a cracked screen.'
expected: Empathetic apology, offer the replacement or refund process, ask for photos of the damage and the order number, mention next steps clearly.

input: Customer says: 'The shirt I ordered has a hole near the seam.'
expected: Apology, offer a return and replacement, ask for the order number and a photo of the defect, do not blame the customer.

input: Customer says: 'Let me speak to a manager. This is the third time I have been transferred.'
expected: Acknowledge the frustration, apologize for the repeated transfers, offer to escalate to a supervisor, ask for the case number to ensure continuity.

input: Customer says: 'I will sue if I do not get my money back today.'
expected: De-escalate calmly, take the concern seriously, offer to escalate to a supervisor, do not make legal commitments or panic-promise a refund.

input: Customer says: 'My laptop arrived with a small scratch on the lid but otherwise works fine.'
expected: Apology, offer partial credit or full return options, let the customer choose, ask for the order number and a photo, do not over-promise.

input: Customer says: 'I entered the wrong shipping address by accident. Can you change it?'
expected: Acknowledge the mistake, offer to update the address if the order has not shipped, ask for the order number and the correct address, set expectations if it cannot be changed.

input: Customer says: 'I was billed in USD but I live in Canada. Why?'
expected: Acknowledge the concern, explain that pricing may default to USD and the bank handles conversion, offer to confirm billing currency on the account, do not invent a refund.

input: Customer says: 'I want to cancel some items in my order but keep the rest.'
expected: Confirm the partial cancellation request, ask which items to cancel and the order number, explain that it depends on fulfillment status.
